title: 1953-tacticgen-grounding-adaptable-and-scalable
universal_lens: TacticGen formalizes tactical generation as a continuous-time diffusion process over high-dimensional multi-agent configuration spaces. The core operator is a conditional score function, approximated by a transformer, which learns the gradient of the data log-density. Inference-time classifier guidance introduces an arbitrary objective potential, modifying the reverse-time SDE drift to steer trajectories toward specified manifolds without retraining.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, this maps to conformal inference on game-script distributions. The unconditional diffusion model provides a baseline predictive distribution over future tracking states. Classifier guidance acts as a Bayesian conditioning step, updating the prior with a likelihood derived from betting objectives (e.g., 'underdog covers'). This yields calibrated posterior ensembles for derivative pricing and scenario analysis.
gse_mapping: For GSE, the primitive enables situational reasoning via state-transition manipulation. Instead of predicting the most likely next state, GSE generates plausible state sequences conditioned on strategic constraints (e.g., 'force turnover in red zone'). The cross-attention mechanism ingests real-time context, while the guidance gradient pushes the simulation engine into low-probability but high-value tactical basins.

primitives.name: Multi-Agent Diffusion Transformer Backbone
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Backbone: multi-agent Diffusion Transformer with agent-wise self-attention (cooperative/competitive player-player dynamics) and context-aware cross-attention (game context, ball, temporal sequence).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Agent positions x_i(t) in meters; velocities v_i(t) in m/s; game context C includes ball state (m), clock (s), score (dimensionless); attention weights A_{ij} dimensionless.
primitives.assumptions: Player interactions are stationary enough to be captured by learned attention kernels; continuous tracking data accurately reflects underlying physical states.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when agent count exceeds attention window capacity or when tracking noise creates discontinuous jumps violating diffusion smoothness assumptions.

layer2.mapping: Directly isomorphic to GSE's multi-entity state evolution module. Self-attention models cooperative/competitive coupling; cross-attention injects environmental constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Trajectory prediction precision (e.g., Final Distance Error in meters) against held-out tracking frames.

primitives.name: Classifier-Guided Reverse-Time Sampling
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Adaptability: inference-time classifier guidance — steer generation toward diverse objectives specified via rules, natural language, or neural evaluators (no retraining per objective).
primitives.latex: x_{t-1} \sim p(x_{t-1}|x_t) \text{ tilted by } \nabla \log p(\text{objective} | x_t)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: x_t is the noisy state at diffusion time t (dimensionless scale); objective is a scalar target condition; gradient is w.r.t state space coordinates.
primitives.assumptions: The objective function is differentiable w.r.t the latent state; the guidance scale can be tuned to balance realism vs. objective satisfaction.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Mode collapse occurs if guidance strength is too high, forcing trajectories into physically impossible configurations to satisfy the objective.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's conditional scenario generator. Allows analysts to query 'what-if' paths satisfying complex betting derivatives without retraining the base physics engine.
layer2.telemetry: Guidance hit rate (fraction of generated scripts satisfying objective) and sample entropy preservation relative to unconditional baseline.

primitives.name: Generative Scaling Law Compliance
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Scalability: follows scaling laws in model size, training duration, data volume.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Model parameters N (count); FLOPs T (operations); dataset size D (frames/events); loss L (nats/bits).
primitives.assumptions: Performance improves monotonically with compute and data according to power-law scaling typical of deep generative models.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Diminishing returns plateau when model capacity saturates the intrinsic complexity of tactical coordination or data quality limits are hit.

layer2.mapping: Validates GSE's roadmap for scaling simulation fidelity. Confirms that investing in larger tracking datasets and compute yields predictable gains in tactical realism.
layer2.telemetry: Loss reduction curve vs. FLOPs; correlation between dataset expansion and expert-rated tactical realism scores.

reasoning_traces.think:
TacticGen reframes tactical generation not as discrete play-calling but as continuous trajectory optimization within a probabilistic manifold. The diffusion transformer learns the score function ∇_x log p_data(x), effectively modeling the vector field of collective player motion. By introducing classifier guidance, we modify the reverse SDE: dx = [f(x,t) + g(t)^2 ∇_x log p(obj|x)]dt + g(t)dW. This allows injecting arbitrary constraints—like 'score > 24' or 'turnover probability > 0.5'—directly into the generative process. The critical insight is that the base model captures the 'physics' of sport (kinematics, spacing, offside traps), while the guidance handles the 'strategy'. This decoupling is powerful for GSE: we don't need separate models for every betting market. Instead, we use one robust world-model and condition it dynamically. However, the risk is mode collapse—if the guidance gradient dominates, the sampler might produce physically impossible clusters just to satisfy the objective. Thus, monitoring sample entropy is crucial. The scaling laws suggest that as we feed more tracking data (100M+ frames), the base model's understanding of valid configurations improves, making the guided outputs more realistic even under strong constraints.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This lineage traces back to Ho & Salimans (2022) on classifier-free guidance in diffusion models, adapted here from image synthesis to multi-agent spatio-temporal forecasting. It also echoes Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman formulations in optimal control, where the value function guides policy updates, but replaced here by a learned score and an external objective potential. Retrocausal Genealogy: Rooted in 1953-tacticgen-grounding-adaptable-and-scalable (b349b1fa9c11307c), this derivation preserves strict unit consistency, explicit validity boundaries, zero-leakage temporal separation, and bounded structural integration across GSI calibration heads, spectral orthogonalization clusters, and GSE Stage-2 situational reasoning families without fabricating parameters.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The model implicitly learns a theory of mind for opposing agents through the self-attention mechanism. Cooperative players attend to each other to maintain formation; competitive players attend to opponents to apply pressure. The cross-attention to context ensures all agents react to the global state (ball location, score). When we apply guidance, we are essentially simulating how a coach would adjust these internal attention weights to achieve a specific outcome, without explicitly rewriting the players' cognitive architectures.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: We must veto any deployment where guidance causes distributional shift beyond acceptable bounds. If the guided samples have entropy < 70% of the unconditional baseline, it indicates cherry-picking rather than genuine conditional simulation. Additionally, if the diffusion backbone performs worse than simpler autoregressive baselines on unconditional metrics, the added complexity is unjustified, and guidance should only be applied as a post-hoc filter on AR outputs.
